topic: The Mechanics of Change: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules
target_audience: High school seniors or first-year university calculus students

outline.topic: The Mechanics of Change: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules
outline.target_audience: High school seniors or first-year university calculus students

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Rate of Change
sections.content: A 45-second refresher on the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change. Visually represent a simple function f(x) = x² and its tangent line. Introduce the concept that functions are often built from simpler parts—either by multiplying them or nesting them inside each other.
sections.example: An animation of a growing square where the side length 'x' increases, showing the area change rate is 2x.

sections.title: The Product Rule: The Expanding Rectangle
sections.content: Explain how to differentiate the product of two functions, f(x) * g(x). Use a geometric visualization: a rectangle with sides 'u' and 'v'. If both sides grow, the total area change is (u * dv) + (v * du). Duration: 75 seconds.
sections.example: Consider a 'Smart Garden' robot that plants seeds. The rate of planting depends on the number of robotic arms (u) times the speed of each arm (v). If both increase, the total rate is: (Arms × Change in Speed) + (Speed × Change in Arms).

sections.title: The Chain Rule: The Nested Gear System
sections.content: Introduce function composition f(g(x)). Visualize this as a system of two connected gears (an outer gear and an inner gear). The Chain Rule states that the overall rate of change is the product of the rates of each part: f'(g(x)) * g'(x). Duration: 90 seconds.
sections.example: A 'Speedy Snail' character moving inside a moving train. The snail's speed relative to the ground is the 'Snail's speed relative to the train' multiplied by the 'Train's speed relative to the ground'.

sections.title: Combined Application: The Jet-Pack Penguin
sections.content: Demonstrate a complex problem requiring both rules. This 60-second segment shows how to identify which rule to apply first (the 'order of operations' for derivatives). Use a layered graphical approach where the outer 'shell' is differentiated first.
sections.example: A Penguin's altitude is defined by H(t) = t² * sin(t³). To find the velocity, we use the Product Rule for (t²) * (sin(t³)), and within that, the Chain Rule for the derivative of sin(t³).

sections.title: Visual Summary and Cheat Sheet
sections.content: A final 30-second recap. Provide a side-by-side visual comparison: Product Rule = 'Addition of Growth' (uv' + vu'), Chain Rule = 'Multiplication of Links' (outer' * inner'). Fade out with the formulas clearly displayed over a moving coordinate plane.
sections.example: Graphic icons: A 'plus' sign for Product Rule and a 'link chain' icon for Chain Rule to cement memory.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Rate of Change
lecture_lines: Derivatives represent the instantaneous rate of change.
For f(x) equals x squared, the rate is 2x.
Complex functions are built from simpler mathematical parts.
animations: Draw a white (#FFFFFF) parabola y = x^2 and a point (x, y).
Add a yellow (#FFFF00) tangent line at (x, y) labeled 'Instantaneous Slope'.
Morph graph into a blue (#0000FF) square expanding by dx with area change 2x.

storyboard.title: The Product Rule: The Expanding Rectangle
lecture_lines: The product rule handles two functions multiplied together.
Imagine a rectangle with expanding side lengths u and v.
The area change depends on both growth rates.
It's u times v-prime plus v times u-prime.
Robots use this to calculate total planting rates.
animations: Draw a rectangle with sides u (red #FF0000) and v (blue #0000FF).
Expand width by du, creating a new area v * du (light red #FF7F7F).
Expand height by dv, creating a new area u * dv (light blue #7F7FFF).
Highlight the two added area strips and sum them: u * dv + v * du.
Write the formula (uv)' = u * v' + v * u' in white (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: The Chain Rule: The Nested Gear System
lecture_lines: The chain rule differentiates nested, or composed, functions.
Visualize an inner gear driving a larger outer gear.
Total speed is the product of individual rates.
Multiply the outer derivative by the inner derivative.
Like a snail's speed relative to the moving ground.
animations: Display nested gears: inner g (green #00FF00) and outer f (magenta #FF00FF).
Rotate inner gear g to show its rate g'(x).
Rotate outer gear f showing its rate relative to g: f'(g(x)).
Connect the gears to show total speed is the product of rates.
Display the formula [f(g(x))]' = f'(g(x)) * g'(x) in white (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Combined Application: The Jet-Pack Penguin
lecture_lines: Some problems require both the product and chain rules.
Meet our jet-pack penguin with a complex altitude function.
Identify the outer product of two distinct functions first.
Apply the product rule while nesting the chain rule.
Solve systematically by peeling back each mathematical layer.
animations: Write H(t) = t^2 * sin(t^3). Color t^2 red (#FF0000) and sin(t^3) blue (#0000FF).
Expand using Product Rule: (t^2)' * sin(t^3) + t^2 * (sin(t^3))'.
Differentiate t^2 to 2t and sin(t^3) using Chain Rule.
Show the inner derivative (t^3)' = 3t^2 being multiplied to cos(t^3).
Simplify and display the full derivative H'(t) in white (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Visual Summary and Cheat Sheet
lecture_lines: Product rule adds the growth of two combined parts.
Chain rule multiplies the links of nested functions.
Master these mechanics to solve any complex derivative.
animations: Show a 'Plus' icon (#FFFF00) for Product and 'Links' icon (#00FFFF) for Chain.
List both formulas (uv)' = uv' + vu' and (f ∘ g)' = f'(g)g'.
Fade out all elements to show 'The Mechanics of Change' in white (#FFFFFF).
